# Reference Corpus Provenance

This directory is committed reference material for the sergeant-rs prototype. It is
evidence, not source: nothing in here is built, imported, or executed by the crate.

| Item | Source | Pinned at | Date vendored |
|---|---|---|---|
| `proposal-depot-rust-execution-surface.md` | User-supplied proposal ("Depot — Rust-Native Agent Execution Surface") | document dated 2026-08-08 | 2026-08-08 |
| `sergeant-upstream/` | https://github.com/miztertea/sergeant (fork of https://github.com/callmeradical/sergeant) | `f430cfd4f90174a98adbd7abebbece6303817929` (main, includes merged PR #2 — Claude background harness) | 2026-08-08 |
| `notes/` | Distillations written for this prototype (sources cited inline) | — | 2026-08-08 |
| `proposal-next-iteration-icm-workflows.md` | Owner-supplied successor proposal ("Sergeant-rs Next Iteration: Measured ICM Workflows and Portable Execution"), delivered via the owner's IdeaOS Drive corpus | document dated 2026-08-10, audited against repo revision `27c00ef` | 2026-08-10 |

Why the fork rather than the original: the fork is a superset containing the measured
Claude background-harness research spike (`sergeant-upstream/docs/research/claude-background-harness-spike.md`),
its PRD (`sergeant-upstream/docs/prds/claude-background-harness.md`), and the fake-CLI
test suite (`sergeant-upstream/tests/sgt-claude-*.sh`) — all direct inputs to this
prototype's Claude backend adapter.

repository is **sergeant-rs** (binary `sgt`) by explicit owner decision, 2026-08-08.

deviations are logged in `GAUNTLET.md` with rationale.

1	# repo-to-icm — workflow orientation
2	
3	Layer 1 (`docs/icm/convention.md` §1a). This file orients an actor entering
4	this workflow for the first time; it is **not** stage instruction — no
5	stage may substitute reading this for its own `CONTEXT.md` contract, and
6	only the first stage lists this file in its Inputs table (§1a rule 5).
7	
8	## What this workflow does
9	
10	`repo-to-icm` (proposal §9.1) converts a repository's distributed
11	procedural knowledge — skills, agent instructions, scripts, docs, tests —
12	into **draft** ICM workflow packages plus an evidence-backed report. It
13	never publishes a workflow into `.sergeant/workflows/`, never edits the
14	engine, and never assumes every source artifact deserves an ICM artifact.
15	Its output is reviewable evidence for a human (or a later, separately
16	reviewed generator run) to promote — nothing this workflow writes is
17	runnable procedure until a human crosses the publication boundary
18	(`docs/icm/convention.md` §2).
19	
20	## The blindness rule (read before touching anything)
21	
22	This run's central safety constraint — for a **measurement** run, every
23	stage's actor is blind to `reference-corpus/`, full stop — is stage
24	instruction, not orientation, so per §1a rule 5 (Layer 1 "MUST NOT contain
25	stage instructions") its operative text lives in `_config/run-discipline.md`
26	(Layer 3), which every stage's own Inputs table names, not here. What
27	follows is orientation only: expect every stage to be bound by it for the
28	whole time it runs, and expect a fail-closed `# AMBIGUOUS — NOT RESOLVED`
29	marker (same file, §2) to propagate down the pipeline rather than be
30	silently papered over if `00-contract` ever has to fail closed instead of
31	guessing.
32	
33	## How the stages hand off
34	
35	Every stage is an ordinary actor stage (§9.2) — a fresh execution per
36	stage, given exactly that stage's own pinned context plus the worktree.
37	There is no shared conversation state between stages; everything one
38	stage needs from an earlier one is a **named Layer-4 artifact**: the
39	producing stage writes it under its own `output/`, and every consuming
40	stage names it explicitly in its own `CONTEXT.md` Inputs table
41	(`docs/icm/record-shapes.md` §1a). An artifact a later stage needs but
42	does not name in its Inputs table is not available to it by convention,
43	whatever a fresh agent might be tempted to go looking for in the
44	worktree.
45	
46	```text
47	00-contract      → output/: repository revision, scope, exclusions,
48	                   output paths, success criteria
49	10-inventory     → output/: deterministic source inventory (decompose /
50	                   helper-evidence / obsolete-candidate / reference-only)
51	20-harvest       → output/: source-cited behavior units (NDJSON, no ICM
52	                   form assigned yet), a per-partition checkpoint ledger,
53	                   and a consequence-class sweep record
54	30-normalize     → output/: the same units rewritten independent of old
55	                   filenames and mechanisms
56	40-classify      → output/: one classification record per behavior unit,
57	                   ladder rung + rationale + alternatives considered
58	50-synthesize    → output/: clustered workflow / stage / context / helper
59	                   / invariant candidates
60	60-draft         → output/: materialized draft workflow package(s) under
61	                   .sergeant/drafts/workflows/, plus provenance.md
62	70-lint          → output/: validator results + any mechanical repairs
63	80-adversarial-review → output/: challenge findings (coverage gaps,
64	                   over-staging, hidden translation, speculative gaps)
65	90-reconcile     → output/: adjudicated findings + final measurement
66	                   package; runs scripts/finalize.py as its closing act
67	```
68	
69	Each stage's own `output/README.md` declares its expected artifact(s) and
70	a **disposition** — `promote` (survives this run's own Work-branch merge)
71	or `evidence` (Work-branch record only). This workflow's outputs are
72	per-run artifacts: the finalize convention (`docs/icm/convention.md` §1a,
73	D9) applies to *this workflow's own* stage outputs at the end of a run,
74	not to the generated draft packages' own (empty, templated) `output/`
75	directories, which describe artifact shape for that *candidate's* future
76	runs, not this one.
77	
78	## Stages
79	
80	| Stage | Durable outcome (§9.3) |
81	|---|---|
82	| `00-contract` | Repository revision, scope, exclusions, output paths, and success criteria are established. |
83	| `10-inventory` | A deterministic inventory of behavioral artifacts exists; unreadable/generated/vendor regions are identified and excluded. |
84	| `20-harvest` | Source-cited behavior units are extracted, without assigning ICM forms yet. |
85	| `30-normalize` | Behavior units are rewritten independently of source filenames and old-implementation mechanisms. |
86	| `40-classify` | The ICM decomposition ladder (`_config/icm-ladder.md`) is applied to every unit, with rationale and alternatives recorded. |
87	| `50-synthesize` | Classified units are clustered into workflow, stage, context, helper, and invariant candidates. |
88	| `60-draft` | Draft workflow package(s) and catalog entries are materialized under the draft namespace. |
89	| `70-lint` | `scripts/validate-structure.py` is run against the drafted package(s); malformed metadata, broken references, duplicate identities, and missing provenance are repaired. |
90	| `80-adversarial-review` | A fresh execution challenges coverage, over-staging, hidden file-shape translation, and speculative engine-gap claims. |
91	| `90-reconcile` | Findings are adjudicated, the final measurement package is emitted, and `scripts/finalize.py` applies this run's own disposition policy. |
92	
93	## Shared config (`_config/`, Layer 3)
94	
95	- `_config/run-discipline.md` — the blindness rule and the
96	  `# AMBIGUOUS — NOT RESOLVED` fail-closed propagation convention. Named in
97	  every stage's own Inputs table (not just `00-contract`'s), since it binds
98	  every stage for the whole run, not only the first one.
99	- `_config/evidence-policy.md` — the citation/quote/hash discipline every
100	  stage that touches a behavior unit (`20-harvest` onward) must follow.
101	- `_config/icm-ladder.md` — the §6 decomposition ladder distilled for
102	  `40-classify`, including the §6.3 reimplementation test and the full
103	  §6.7 engine-gap template.
104	
105	## Helpers (`scripts/`)
106	
107	- `scripts/validate-structure.py` — the §9.7 structural validator. Run with
108	  no arguments it checks this workflow's own tree; given a path, it checks
109	  a generated draft tree (used by `70-lint`).
110	- `scripts/finalize.py` — the D9 disposition finalize helper, run once by
111	  `90-reconcile` at the close of a run. It is deterministic machinery
112	  (`docs/icm/convention.md` §5): it reads dispositions, it does not decide
113	  whether an artifact should exist — that judgment belongs to the stage
114	  that wrote it. Before removing anything it now verifies every file it is
115	  about to remove is already reachable in a committed tree, and refuses
116	  outright (fail-closed, nothing modified) rather than deleting a file that
117	  was never actually committed — see the module docstring and
118	  `docs/gauntlet/runs/n2-run2/grammar-pressure-report.md` GP-5b.
119	- `scripts/test-finalize-evidence-guard.py` — a standalone sandbox test
120	  proving `finalize.py`'s evidence-preservation guard holds in both
121	  directions (refuses on an uncommitted file, proceeds on a committed one).
122	  Not invoked by any stage; run by a human or CI directly, and by
123	  `validate-structure.py`'s `[S15]` check against this workflow's own tree.
124	
125	All three are helpers subordinate to their invoking stage's judgment
126	(`docs/icm/convention.md` §5) — their exit status and structured output are
127	something the actor reviews and acts on, not something the engine
128	interprets on its own. A stage invoking one of the first two states the
129	exact repository-root-relative invocation and this run's working-directory
130	convention in its own `CONTEXT.md` (see `70-lint` and `90-reconcile`) — this
131	orientation file does not itself hand a stranger an executable command.
132	
133	## v2: how `20-harvest` handles volume (read before assuming one turn is enough)
134	
135	N2 run 2 covered 16 of 136 `decompose`-dispositioned files in one `20-harvest`
136	turn before its context window closed (`docs/gauntlet/runs/n2-run2/
137	grammar-pressure-report.md` GP-1). The adjudicated fix is authoring
138	guidance, not an engine change — two shapes were weighed:
139	
140	- **Rejected: split `20-harvest` into a fixed sequence of numbered
141	  partition-slice stages** (e.g. `20a-harvest-p1` … `20e-harvest-p5`, one
142	  per `10-inventory` partition, each a genuinely fresh actor turn). This
143	  requires committing, at workflow-*authoring* time, to a maximum partition
144	  count — but `10-inventory/CONTEXT.md` is explicit that this workflow "is
145	  not scoped to any one repository shape," so the partition count a future
146	  subject repository's inventory produces is unbounded and unknowable in
147	  advance. A repository whose inventory yields more partitions than the
148	  provisioned slots reproduces the identical volume-wall failure this fix
149	  exists to close, merely relocated to a higher, less visible threshold —
150	  and every slot a smaller repository doesn't need is a wasted stage
151	  directory, `CONTEXT.md`, Inputs table, and `output/README.md` to author
152	  and maintain. It also multiplies engine-visible stage identity for
153	  something that fails §6.3's own reimplementation test applied to the
154	  *stage boundary itself*: "harvest partition 3" is not a checkpoint
155	  operators would care about independently of "harvest partition 1" — it is
156	  the same checkpoint kind repeated, homogeneous iteration inside one
157	  parent, not distinct procedural structure (the same conclusion
158	  grammar-pressure-report.md's §21.8 section reaches: this is iteration, not
159	  workflow composition).
160	- **Chosen: keep `20-harvest` as the single stage it already is, and give it
161	  an explicit per-partition checkpoint-and-retry protocol** (below). This
162	  matches a mechanism the engine already ships and that run 2's own journal
163	  exercised (by accident, via a different bug) and proved works: a stage
164	  that cannot finish within one turn stops cleanly at a partition boundary,
165	  writes a durable, `promote`d partition ledger recording exactly which
166	  partitions are done and which remain, and is re-entered as a **fresh
167	  execution** — fresh actor turn, fresh context window — via `sgt work
168	  retry`, picking up from the ledger rather than starting over. This scales
169	  to however many partitions a given repository's inventory actually
170	  produces, with no author-time upper bound, at the cost of relying on a
171	  human (or an orchestrating caller) to notice an incomplete ledger and
172	  issue the retry — which is the same shape `00-contract`'s own fail-closed
173	  `# AMBIGUOUS — NOT RESOLVED` marker already relies on (a human or caller
174	  acting on a durable, explicit signal this workflow writes, not a new
175	  engine primitive). It does **not** depend on the actor-initiated
176	  mid-turn ask primitive GP-2 confirms is not yet wired to a real harness —
177	  the actor never tries to pause *inside* a turn; it simply ends its turn
178	  early and honestly, the same way `10-inventory`'s existing "On volume"
179	  section already does for a single-turn stage.
180	
181	`20-harvest/CONTEXT.md` and `20-harvest/references/partition-checkpoint-
182	protocol.md` carry the operative version of this protocol; `_config/
183	icm-ladder.md` and this file are the record of the choice.
184

1	# Run discipline — blindness and fail-closed propagation
2	
3	Layer 3 (`_config/`), stable across every run, shared by **every** stage of
4	this workflow (`00-contract` through `90-reconcile` — every stage's own
5	`## Inputs` table names this file). Two rules that apply to the whole run,
6	not to any one stage's own contract: the blindness boundary, and how a
7	stage must react if an upstream artifact reports itself unresolved.
8	
9	Moved here (from the workflow-level `../CONTEXT.md`, Layer 1) because Layer
10	1 orients and is not stage instruction, and the engine does not deliver it
11	to any stage past the first (`docs/icm/convention.md` §1a rule 5) — a rule
12	every stage must actually follow cannot live somewhere only one stage's
13	Inputs table names. `../CONTEXT.md` still summarizes both rules for a human
14	skimming the workflow; this file is the operative version an actor's own
15	stage contract actually points at.
16	
17	## 1. The blindness rule
18	
19	If this run's purpose is **measurement** — comparing generated output

# Run discipline — blindness and fail-closed propagation

Layer 3 (`_config/`), stable across every run, shared by **every** stage of
this workflow (`00-contract` through `90-reconcile` — every stage's own
`## Inputs` table names this file). Two rules that apply to the whole run,
not to any one stage's own contract: the blindness boundary, and how a
stage must react if an upstream artifact reports itself unresolved.

Moved here (from the workflow-level `../CONTEXT.md`, Layer 1) because Layer
1 orients and is not stage instruction, and the engine does not deliver it
to any stage past the first (`docs/icm/convention.md` §1a rule 5) — a rule
every stage must actually follow cannot live somewhere only one stage's
Inputs table names. `../CONTEXT.md` still summarizes both rules for a human
skimming the workflow; this file is the operative version an actor's own
stage contract actually points at.

## 1. The blindness rule

If this run's purpose is **measurement** — comparing generated output
against an already-adjudicated reference decomposition (as in the N2
measurement run against `reference/sergeant-upstream`, graded against
`reference-corpus/`) — then for the entire run, every stage's actor is
**blind to `reference-corpus/`**: never open it, never grep it, never let
it enter a prompt, never let a helper's output surface its contents. This
is not a preference; contaminating the run with the answer key invalidates
the measurement it exists to produce (`docs/gauntlet/contracts/N2.md`
Outcome §2). A stage that needs to check its own output's shape uses
`../scripts/validate-structure.py`, never `reference-corpus/lint.py` or any
file under `reference-corpus/` — those are the graders' tools, applied
*after* this run completes, by a separate comparison process this
workflow's actors do not perform. If a stage's actor is ever tempted to
peek "just to check the shape," that temptation is itself the signal to
stop and re-read this paragraph.

Outside a measurement run (e.g. a first decomposition of a repository with
no existing reference corpus), this rule is vacuous — there is nothing to
be blind to — but the discipline it enforces (cite only the *target*
repository under decomposition, never a pre-existing answer) still holds:
never source a behavior unit's `quote` from anywhere but the repository
this run is decomposing.

This is the run's central safety constraint, not a suggestion any one
stage can treat as background context — every stage listed above is bound
by it for the whole time it is executing, whether or not its own
`CONTEXT.md` restates it inline.

## 2. Fail-closed propagation: the `# AMBIGUOUS — NOT RESOLVED` marker

`00-contract`'s own contract requires it to fail closed rather than guess
when the subject repository, revision, or scope is ambiguous — and, because
the current engine gives no actor stage a way to pause its turn and wait
for a human answer, the fail-closed action available to it is to write
`output/contract.md` anyway, headed:

```text
# AMBIGUOUS — NOT RESOLVED
```

**Every stage from `10-inventory` onward: before doing any of your own
stage's work, check whether the upstream artifact(s) named in your own
Inputs table open with this exact heading.** If any does:

1. Do not proceed with your stage's ordinary work — do not invent a subject,
   revision, scope, or any other fact the unresolved artifact was supposed
   to establish.
2. Write your own stage's declared `output/` artifact(s) starting with the
   same `# AMBIGUOUS — NOT RESOLVED` heading, so the marker chains
   mechanically through every later hop without each stage having to sniff
   free-form prose for it. Under the heading, name which upstream artifact
   you found it in and quote its "What is ambiguous" line — do not
   originate a new explanation; you are relaying, not re-diagnosing.
3. Stop. Do not attempt an ordinary durable outcome you were not given the
   facts to reach honestly.

This propagation is itself the run's fail-closed behavior end to end: one
stage's honest "I could not resolve this" turns into every downstream
stage's honest "I did not proceed on an unresolved input," rather than a
guess silently compounding through nine more stages.
